get_climate_zone.description: Find a place's ASHRAE 169 climate zone, the one building energy codes use, worked out from NASA's data for a period: a thermal zone from 0 (extremely hot) to 8 (subarctic) and a moisture letter, A (humid), B (dry) or C (marine), such as 3A. Takes about 10 seconds. No API key required.

mock_response.summary: ASHRAE climate zone 3A (warm, humid), from 2016 to 2025.

parameters.description: How far east (positive) or west (negative) of Greenwich, from -180 to 180. For example -76.35 for Hampton, Virginia.
parameters.name: longitude

parameters.description: The first year to work the zone out from, from 1981.
parameters.name: start_year

parameters.name: end_year

NASA's standard period runs from 2001 to the latest full year; give a start and end year for another one. Up to 20 parameters per step. No API key required.

description: NASA's free solar, weather and climate data for any point on Earth: hourly, daily and monthly temperature, sunlight, rain, wind, humidity and over a hundred more values from 1981 to the last few days, long-term averages, values across a whole region, wind roses, ASHRAE climate zones and building design conditions. Used for solar energy, agriculture and building design. No account or API key required.
